[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Number of longest increasing subsequences** [LC 673 · Number of Longest Increasing Subsequence](https://leetcode.com/problems/number-of-longest-increasing-subsequence/){difficulty="Medium"}

The length ending at $i$ is the LIS recurrence. The count is carried beside it. A predecessor that makes a strictly longer chain replaces the count, because every old way of reaching $i$ is now too short. A predecessor that ties the best length adds its count. Summing the counts of every shorter predecessor over-counts: those chains are not longest.

[Solved in full in @sec-lis-p1-count.]{.card-link}
